text:
alex: Heads-up: shadow benchmark for PR 12811 is failing the microbench threshold on small-batch path. p95 +12%, p99 +18% vs main. failing job: ci/shadow/bench-smallbatch (link: https://ci.redwood/495123)

nina: ack. saw an alert this morning. any obvious diffs in the trace?

perf-ci-bot: benchmark: shadow/bench-smallbatch
status: FAILED
baseline: p99=42.1ms
current: p99=49.7ms (+18.1%)
regression metric: small_batch_tail_latency
rerun_cmd: ./scripts/bench --suite smallbatch --repeat 10 --pr 12811

jamie: ran the rerun locally against the same hw, reproduced ~+15% p99.
quick profile snapshot attached to CI: kernel_autoselect chose fallback kernel for seq=64 in ~30% of calls (was 2% on main).

kevin: that matches KV cache telemetry I pulled: hitrate dropped from 91% -> 63% for the shadow workload after the change in batching heuristics. More coldpath entries, which triggers slower kernels.

alex: commit that merged before the PR build: 7a1f2b3 changed the prefetch/batcher window heuristics and also tightened quantization fallback thresholds. suspect interaction between prefetch window and KV warmup sequence.

nina: can we bisect quickly? either the batching tweak or the quantization threshold change would explain kernel_autoselect flip.

jamie: bisect notes:
- base (main at ~4950000000): kernel_autoselect fallback rate 2%, kv_hitrate 91%
- merge 7a1f2b3 (batcher tweak): fallback rate -> 18%, kv_hitrate 68%
- followup 9c3d4e5 (quant threshold): fallback rate -> 30%, kv_hitrate 63%
Looks like 7a1f2b3 introduced most of the change; 9c3d4e5 amplified it.

kevin: reproduction script I used:
```
# reproduce perf microbench
git checkout 7a1f2b3~1 && ./scripts/bench --suite smallbatch --hw A100 --runs 20 > out_base.log
git checkout 7a1f2b3 && ./scripts/bench --suite smallbatch --hw A100 --runs 20 > out_7a.log
python tools/compare_latency.py out_base.log out_7a.log
```
Comparisons show coldpath ratio jump correlates with higher p99.

alex: rollout blocked. can we do a targeted revert of the prefetch window tweak as a mitigation while we fix heuristics? We should avoid reverting quant thresholds until we understand interaction.

nina: +1 for targeted revert. I've opened revert PR 12817 that reverts the prefetch window change only. request review from infra and runtime owners.

perf-ci-bot: triggered job: ci/shadow/bench-smallbatch on PR 12817 (revert) queued.

jamie: quick patch idea instead of revert: relax prefetch aggressiveness for seq<=128 and increase backoff on batcher ramp-up. that should keep KV warmup stable for short sequences. I can prototype and bench.

kevin: one more datapoint: when we force kernel selector to prefer the optimized kernel (override env KERNEL_FORCE=optimized) p99 on the patched PR drops back near baseline even with reduced cache hitrate. So two levers: keep kernel preferred or restore KV warmup. Prefer fixing warmup to avoid masking underlying cost.

alex: sounds good. action items:
- nina: shepherd revert PR 12817 to block rollout (in flight)
- jamie: prototype batcher tweak (ramp/backoff) and bench in shadow; post results here
- kevin: collect KV cache histograms (per seq len) for main, 7a1f2b3, and revert
- perf-ci-bot: run shadow bench on revert PR and post results

jamie: I'll post a microbench log within 2 hours. ping me for infra help.

nina: looks like revert PR passed initial shadow bench (ci/shadow/bench-smallbatch) -> p99=43.0ms. still slightly higher than baseline but within threshold. holding rollout blocked until followups merged. :lock:

alex: thanks all. let's avoid a full revert if we can land a narrower hotfix, but good call to block rollout. keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
